title: The Rotated Signal

story.briefing: The channel array was rotated during the outage. It is still sorted, just not from the beginning, and the correct channel has to be found without sweeping the whole thing.
story.success: Channel located through the rotation. Communications come back online.

description: An array of distinct values was sorted in increasing order, then rotated left by some unknown amount — so [1, 3, 5, 7] might arrive as [5, 7, 1, 3]. A rotation of zero is possible. Given such an array and a target, return the index of the target, or -1 if it is absent.

examples.explanation: A rotation of zero is still valid input.

hints: Cut the array anywhere and at least one of the two halves is still in plain sorted order. Work out which one, every time.
Once you know which half is sorted, you can tell whether the target lies inside it by comparing against that half endpoints — and if it does not, it must be in the other half.

Compare the middle with the left end. If the left half is sorted and the target sits between the left value and the middle, search left; otherwise search right. If instead the right half is sorted, apply the mirror image of that test.
